title: Blocked tracheostomy
stem: Resus 3. A 67-year-old man with a tracheostomy (inserted 3 weeks ago after a long ICU stay) has come from a rehabilitation ward. He is in respiratory distress. HR 124, BP 150/90, RR 34, SpO2 84% on oxygen via the tracheostomy mask. The bed-head sign says: 'Tracheostomy — patent upper airway. Cuffed tube with inner cannula.' Manage him.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Monitoring on; tracheostomy or laryngectomy? Look, listen, feel, capnography.

phases.title: Help and oxygen
phases.goal: The airway team, and oxygen to the right places.

phases.title: Is it patent?
phases.goal: Work through the tracheostomy yourself, in order; then keep it clear.

phases.title: Plan B
phases.goal: The examiner asks what if suction had failed.

notes:
Checked against the National Tracheostomy Safety Project (NTSP) emergency algorithms (UK, 2012 with later updates) and current HK hospital practice.

First, is it a tracheostomy (upper airway still connects to the lungs) or a laryngectomy (a neck breather, no connection)? The bed-head sign tells you. With a tracheostomy you can oxygenate from both the face and the stoma, and intubate orally if needed; with a laryngectomy only the stoma works.

NTSP sequence: call for help (airway expert); look, listen and feel at the mouth and the tracheostomy; high-flow oxygen to both the face and the stoma; waveform capnography on the tracheostomy. Is it patent? Remove the speaking valve or cap; remove the inner cannula; pass a suction catheter. If the catheter will not pass, deflate the cuff. If he is still not improving, remove the tracheostomy tube. Then: breathing? Oxygen to face and stoma. Not breathing? Start CPR and ventilate via the mouth (occlude the stoma) or via the stoma with a paediatric mask or supraglottic airway. Secondary: oral intubation with an uncut tube advanced beyond the stoma, or a small tube (6.0) or bougie via the stoma.

Your tracheostomy notes follow this order; they add confirming placement with capnography, auscultation and fibreoptic view, which is correct. For bleeding (possible tracheo-innominate fistula), your notes are also correct: over-inflate the cuff, compress through the stoma against the sternum, and do not remove the tube until the airway is secured below the bleed.

Perfect script checked against the NTSP algorithm, an ATLS/DAS airway checklist, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong options (face-mask oxygen only, mouth oxygen after laryngectomy) and the bench's 'bag hard' and 'pull the whole tube out' buttons. Added: care once patent and a tracheostomy review.

qs.a: Bed-head sign; is the upper airway connected?
wrong: The colour of the tube and flange
The size of the stoma alone

qs.a: Over-inflate the cuff; press on the stoma

rules.fail: You worked on the tube without checking whether it is a tracheostomy or a laryngectomy.

badge.name: Stoma Saver
badge.flavor: Read the sign. Inner cannula out before the tube comes out.

cards.q: In a tracheostomy emergency, oxygen goes to…
options: Both the face and the stoma
The face only
The stoma only
Neither until a new tube is in
cards.why: The upper airway is still patent in a tracheostomy.

cards.q: In a laryngectomy patient, oxygen goes to…
options: The stoma only
The face only
Both
A nasal cannula
cards.why: No connection between the upper airway and the trachea.

cards.q: First patency step in a blocked tracheostomy?
options: Remove the speaking valve and inner cannula
Remove the whole tube at once
Give nebulised saline and wait
Increase the cuff pressure to 40 cmH2O
cards.why: Most blockages are in the inner cannula.

cards.q: If a suction catheter will not pass down the tracheostomy…
options: Deflate the cuff, then consider removal
Push the catheter harder through the block
Bag vigorously through the tracheostomy
Wait for the ENT team before any action
cards.why: The tube may be displaced or blocked.

cards.q: Massive bleeding from a tracheostomy weeks after insertion: first action?
options: Hyper-inflate the cuff and apply pressure
Remove the tube and pack the stoma
Deflate the cuff so blood can drain upwards
Arrange a CT angiogram of the neck first
cards.why: Tamponade the tracheo-innominate fistula while calling for surgery.

cards.q: Tube for oral intubation in a tracheostomy patient?
options: Uncut, advanced beyond the stoma
Cut short at 18 cm at the lips
A nasal tube to avoid the stoma
Size 9.0 cuffless tube, cut to 20 cm
cards.why: The cuff must sit below the stoma.

script.say: Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2. The bed-head sign: a tracheostomy, not a laryngectomy, so the upper airway is patent; cuffed tube with an inner cannula.
Look, listen and feel at the mouth and the tracheostomy: little airflow at the stoma, some at the mouth, chest heaving. Waveform capnography on the tracheostomy: a weak trace.
Call the airway team now, please: the anaesthetist and ENT. High-flow oxygen to both the face and the tracheostomy.
Is it patent? Speaking valve off. Inner cannula out: crusted with secretions. Pass a suction catheter: it goes down easily. A clean inner cannula in, and humidify.

It's patent now and his saturation is rising. Humidified oxygen, regular suction and inner cannula cleaning, capnography on the tracheostomy. ICU outreach and ENT to review the tracheostomy before he goes back to the ward.

If suction had failed: deflate the cuff. If he's still no better, remove the tracheostomy tube. If he's not breathing: CPR; ventilate by mouth with the stoma covered, or via the stoma with a small mask or LMA. Then oral intubation with an uncut tube advanced past the stoma, or a size 6.0 tube through the stoma.
